title: The Fishing Tournament Tragedy
notes: Detective-cast nodes (Conan, Ran, Kogoro, Detective Boys Genta/Mitsuhiko/Ayumi, Inspector Yokomizo) omitted by convention even though several of them perform plot-relevant actions (finding the rigged plank, spotting Ayukawa on the riverbank, conducting interrogations) -- consistent with how ep011 omits the recurring cast performing equivalent functions. The old cases/ file's culprit (Ayukawa Saori) and general mechanism are correct and confirmed by her own confession in the transcript, so no culprit correction was needed here. What the old file missed/flattened, restored in this rebuild: (1) Kanie Kensuke as a distinct backstory victim/person node rather than folded into a single event description -- his death, 6 months prior, used the *same* displaced-crime-scene mechanism (struck near the cliff/train tracks by Kutani Bridge, body later found at the same downstream site) as Funaki's murder, which is a real structural echo the old file's single event line loses; (2) Ayukawa's father as the shared-mentor figure linking Ayukawa, Masubuchi, and Kanie; (3) Masubuchi's romantic motive for arguing with Funaki (red herring, no alibi) as a `has_motive_against` edge rather than leaving him a suspect with no stated reason; (4) the old file's single collapsed object ('wooden plank and rock rigged with a handkerchief and fishing line') split into plank/handkerchief/camera as distinct physical items, since each was recovered/reasoned about independently. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Petroleum/coal stain on Funaki's vest plus an express-train photo in his own recovered camera place him atop the train from Kutani Bridge -- proving his body was carried and dumped, not killed where it was found.

Luminol reacts positive on Ayukawa's handkerchief tied to the rigged plank even though it looks clean -- dried blood survives washing, proving the 'washed' handkerchief was the one used on Ayumi's cut the day before.
